traits.leaf_colour_autumn.note: Wikipedia, Acer circinatum (read 2026-10-18): "the leaves turn bright yellow to orange red". Colour ours, between the two.

generator.params.spur_leaf.note: A short shoot's leaf card, a little smaller than a long shoot's (leaf_size), within Abrams vol. 3 (1951): leaves 7 to 12 cm wide.

generator.params.leaf_size.note: Leaf card length, petiole included, sized so every leaf drawn stays within Abrams vol. 3 (1951, as Acer circinatum): leaves 7 to 12 cm wide (0.16 drew them 17 to 21 cm wide).

traits.flowering_months.note: iNaturalist research-grade records on GBIF in the south and central Puget Sound lowlands (46.7 to 48.0° N, 122.0 to 123.1° W; counted 2026-10-14): 62 records annotated as flowering (Apr 31, May 31); stated as the months holding at least a tenth of them, April and May. FEIS (Acer circinatum) gives April to June.

traits.fruiting_months.note: USA National Phenology Network observations (Nature's Notebook) at lowland sites west of the Cascades in Washington and Oregon (below 300 m, west of 121.8° W; 2009 to 2026, fetched 2026-10-14): 290 plant-years at 48 sites seen with ripe fruit, by the months they were seen in (Jan 25, Feb 10, Mar 3, Apr 1, May 15, Jun 39, Jul 81, Aug 119, Sep 152, Oct 137, Nov 107, Dec 54); stated as the months with at least a third as many as the busiest, July to December. FEIS (Acer circinatum): ripe in September or October, the seed then shed through November; so ripe samaras are on the plant from September to November.

traits.height_max_m.note: Abrams vol. 3 (1951), as Acer circinatum: grows 10 m to 15 m tall.

traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Acer circinatum (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.56 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.56, branches 0.53. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a sprawling shrub or small tree of crooked, leaning stems that root where they touch the ground, with nearly round, seven- to nine-lobed leaves held flat in layers. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 5 m tall at 20 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green leaves, red and orange in autumn; smooth greenish-brown bark. Fruit (plant roadmap P4), as in mid-July: samara pairs with wings spread almost straight apart, red and green. Its year (appearance.organs.bloom.season) takes its days of bud, flower, fruit, ripe and fall from the months it flowers and fruits in, by the rules at the flowering plants (development, 2026-10-14); until then they were authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands: small red-and-white flowers in April and May; samaras red-winged from July, brown in the autumn. The forest's packages show day 196 (mid-July) until the phenology of plant roadmap P5 sets the day from the date and the local climate. Bark pattern (plant roadmap P4, `bark_pattern`): smooth green to reddish-brown bark; set from general knowledge of the species, not measured. Leaf families (plant roadmap P4, `families`): in sun smaller, more deeply cut leaves; in the forest's shade larger, thinner and shallowly lobed ones; set from general knowledge of sun and shade leaves and juvenile foliage, not measured.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

appearance.organs.bloom.season.flower_lo.note: Its flowers drawn one by one (spec rework L1b): small flowers 6 to 9 mm across, red-purple sepals round white petals. From general descriptions of the species (OregonFlora, the Flora of North America and nursery and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read). The size is the flower's width, or a closed corolla's length, over the fruit's length, roughly as in life. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): five petals between five sepals, eight stamens and a pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Sapindaceae and Acer by the rules at the flowering plants.
